dedupe_keys.name: bloodpath agent based model of bloodborne pathogen transmission within hospitals

description: BloodPaTH is an R package whose core, written in C++, is an agent-based model of how bloodborne pathogens such as hepatitis B and C spread inside a hospital. It simulates patients moving between wards from admission to discharge, the use, reuse, contamination and sterilisation of medical devices during invasive procedures, and infection of patients exposed to a contaminated device through a susceptible-exposed-infected model. The provider is Henriot and co-authors, who describe it in PLOS Computational Biology (2025). Coverage is any hospital for which longitudinal admission data and procedure probabilities exist; the paper calibrates it to Ain Shams University Hospital in Cairo for hepatitis C and illustrates hepatitis B in Ethiopia. The code is on GitHub under the GNU GPL version 2 or later, installs in R with devtools, and the latest tag read today is v0.2-alpha. Caveats: the package is an alpha release, results depend on ward transition and procedure data that few hospitals publish, and only device-borne transmission is modelled. Simulation uses: the effect of device shortages in low-resource or disrupted hospitals, where the paper finds frequent shortages raise infection risk, and targeted screening strategies. Related records: H-outbreak (model-h-outbreak) simulates contact-borne hospital outbreaks, and Covasim (model-covasim) models community epidemics.
